shots.title: Warn instead of hard-blocking when slope map cannot refresh without overwriting curated maps (#505)
shots.notes: Removed the deadlock path by making downstream `slope map` preserve existing curated maps and refresh metadata instead of failing or forcing an overwrite.

shots.title: Support metadata-only freshness refresh or broader source detection for non-TypeScript repos (#505)
shots.notes: Broadened source/test counting beyond TS/TSX to include Python, C#, JS, Java, Go, Rust, Ruby, PHP, Swift, Kotlin, and C/C++ while skipping generated, dependency, runtime, and `.slope` directories.

shots.title: Make map staleness baselines worktree-aware to avoid inflated commit counts (#505)
shots.notes: Changed map staleness distance to use `git rev-list --count --ancestry-path`, so sibling worktree or harness base SHAs do not inflate guard blocking counts.

shots.title: Add non-TypeScript curated map, worktree staleness, and Windows map --check regressions (#505)

hazards.description: Parallelized four `slope claim` writes despite the S138 no-parallel-state-write lesson. The claims completed cleanly, but the process hazard was recorded for discipline.

shots.notes: Added regressions for Python/Unity-style source detection, metadata-only curated map refresh, sibling-branch `map --check`, and explore-guard ancestry-path staleness.

conditions.description: The Windows full suite continues to emit known temp-repo stderr and CRLF warnings, but all tests passed.

training.description: Guard recovery commands should preserve user-authored navigation artifacts by default.
training.outcome: Downstream `slope map` now updates metadata or generated sections without replacing curated `CODEBASE.md` content unless `--force` is explicit.

training.description: Raw commit distance is the wrong abstraction for worktree-derived guard blocking.
training.outcome: Both `slope map --check` and the explore guard use ancestry-path distance, avoiding sibling-base inflation while preserving normal ancestor staleness.

nutrition.description: `corepack pnpm vitest run tests/cli/commands/map.test.ts tests/cli/guards/explore.test.ts` passed: 21 tests.

`slope roadmap validate` passed with existing historical roadmap warnings.

nineteenth_hole.how_did_it_feel: Precise and satisfying. The fix landed once the problem was treated as preservation plus staleness math, not merely a threshold tweak.
nineteenth_hole.advice_for_next_player: When a guard suggests a command as the recovery path, test that the command can actually clear the guard without damaging user-authored artifacts.
nineteenth_hole.what_surprised_you: Broadening source detection would have made the old overwrite path more dangerous, so metadata preservation had to come first.
nineteenth_hole.excited_about_next: S143 can apply the same recovery-path mindset to portable sprint resume.

bunker_locations: Do not parallelize SLOPE commands that write sprint or claim state, even when each command targets a different file.
Broader source detection can make an existing overwrite path more dangerous unless preservation semantics are updated first.
Guard staleness checks in worktrees should prefer ancestry-path evidence over raw commit reachability.
yardage_book_updates: `slope map` now preserves existing downstream non-SLOPE-shaped `CODEBASE.md` files by refreshing metadata or marker-delimited generated sections.
`slope map --force` remains the explicit replacement path for downstream maps.
`countSourceFiles` now recognizes non-TypeScript languages and skips dependency, generated, runtime, and `.slope` directories.
`slope map --check` and `exploreGuard` use ancestry-path git distance to avoid sibling worktree base inflation.
course_management_notes: Validation passed: focused S142 tests, adjacent guard/commit-ready tests, `corepack pnpm typecheck`, `corepack pnpm prepare`, `corepack pnpm test`, and `slope roadmap validate`.
